analysis.title: Delta-One Flows & Positioning: Bond rout draws record dip-buyers; Semis de-risking; Managed Money sells commodities (5 October 2026)
key_insights: US bond futures saw the largest weekly net buying in JPM's 5-year history ($89Bn, 3.4z). It fully reversed the prior week's heavy selling, as the rate sell-off triggered aggressive dip-buying.

Fixed income ETFs drew record inflows of $29.6Bn (3.7z) even as yields rose. Munis ($9.1Bn, 6z), government bonds ($6.4Bn, 3.3z, long-term Treasuries $3.3Bn, 2.8z) and money market ($7.8Bn, 1.5z) led. Mortgages saw outflows of $1.2Bn (-2.7z) and IG was weak.

Bond futures liquidity deteriorated sharply in the sell-off. US market depth was about 3-4z below average and EMEA about 5-6z below average. Germany 10y depth was -5.9z, Italy 10y -6.5z and 10y UST -3.6z.

Equity ETF flows were moderately below average at $20.4Bn (-0.4z). US equity flows were near average at $16.5Bn. International was weak in both DM (+$5Bn, -0.6z) and EM (-$1Bn, -1.1z), led by China (-$0.4Bn, -1.2z).

Semis were de-risked. Tech ETFs saw outflows of $3.7Bn (-1.5z), driven by SOXL/SOXX/SMH at -$4.0Bn combined, while SOXS took in +$0.25Bn. SOXX had the largest 1w single-ETF outflow among sector funds at -$2.4Bn.
A large issuer model rebalance rotated money from Financials (-$1.7Bn, -1.4z) into Utilities (+$1.0Bn, +2.6z). Staples also saw outflows (-$0.5Bn, -1.4z).
Option-based ETF strategies drew strong inflows. Defined outcome took ~$0.9Bn (1.6z) and call writing ~$1.6Bn (1.1z). Single stock ETFs took $0.9Bn (0.6z), led by levered AMD/INTC/SNDK products.

Futures flows outside bonds: MSCI EAFE, TOPIX and ASX 200 each saw about 3z net buying. Nikkei, UK and Korea 10y, SOFR and copper futures saw net buying above 1.5z. Dow Jones, Bovespa, soybean and USD/CNH futures saw net selling below -1.5z.

CTAs likely remain net long equities but sold EMEA w/w. They remain broadly short global rates ex-China and likely sold metals incrementally. CTA signal for S&P 500 is Long with the futures at 7,769, Nasdaq 100 Long at 31,000, and VIX futures Short at 17.68.

CFTC data: Asset Managers sold S&P 500 futures (-30,452 contracts, -1.1z) while Leveraged Funds sold EAFE and MID futures. Managed Money broadly sold commodities, led by US natgas (-2.7z), silver (-1.8z) and WTI (-1.5z).

Commodities fell sharply on the week. Gold returned -3.6% and silver -6.0%, with CTA signals Short for gold and neutral for silver. Brent fell 2.0% and WTI 1.4%, with CTAs still long. Natgas fell 5.0%.

Crypto: Bitcoin futures returned +1.0% on the week with CTAs long, and Ether futures -0.4% with CTAs long. Open interest fell 11.3% in Bitcoin and 9.3% in Ether. Crypto ETFs took in $106Mn on the week and $3.5Bn over four weeks.
crypto_views: Bitcoin futures: 1w return +1.0%, OI change -11.3% w/w, 1w net flow 0.7z, CTA signal Long. Ether futures: 1w return -0.4%, OI change -9.3%, CTA Long.
Cryptocurrency ETFs saw $106Mn of net 1w flow (0.0z) and $3,521Mn over 4 weeks (1.0z).

The Zcash ETF (ZCSH) was the top 4w ETF performer at +89.7% but the worst 1w performer at -17.3%. Grayscale Chainlink Trust ETF (GLNK) +25.2% and Bitwise Solana Staking ETF (BSOL) +23.1% were also among the top 4w performers.
COT: Asset Managers net long 3,586 Bitcoin futures contracts (+415 w/w) and Dealers reduced to 2,680 (-967 w/w, -1.8z).
risk_factors: Rates volatility pressured liquidity, with bond futures market depth 3-6z below average, so further rate moves could gap.
Record bond buying into a rising-yield move leaves ETF and futures holders exposed if the sell-off resumes.
Managed Money net selling across commodities and CTA short signals in gold and silver could add pressure if levels slip further.
vol_and_positioning: VIX futures: 1w net flow 0.9z, 1w return +3.0%, CTA signal Short at 17.68 (prior week signal Neutral). Asset Manager VIX futures position is -66,500 (-2.2z).
CTA positioning in US Treasuries is Short across all contracts. 10y UST futures at 104.3 and the long bond at 102.4 sit well below their 50d, 100d and 200d moving averages.

German bund CTA signals (2y, 5y, 10y, 30y) are expected to become less short next week (arrows up) if levels are unchanged. Korea 10y, US natgas, copper and USD/BRL signals also flag a move toward long.
Gold, Brent, gasoline and AUD/USD CTA signals are flagged to turn shorter or less long next week if levels are unchanged.

CFTC leveraged funds are net short 2y UST by 1,165,980 contracts (2.2z, +184,760 w/w), while asset managers cut 2y UST longs by 131,607. In 10y UST, asset managers added 245,147 (2.4z) and dealers cut 155,911 (-2.8z).
CFTC WTI non-commercial net length fell by 31,643 contracts (-1.8z) and Managed Money US natgas shorts grew by 67,252 (-2.7z).
